title: 2003 AMC 12A 13
statement: The polygon enclosed by the solid lines in the figure consists of \(4\) congruent squares joined edge-to-edge. One more congruent square is attached to an edge at one of the nine positions indicated. How many of the nine resulting polygons can be folded to form a cube with one face missing?

solutions.text:
A cube missing one face has \(5\) faces, so the fifth square must fold onto a face not already occupied by the four-square piece. Tracing the face reached by each attachment, positions \(1,\) \(2,\) and \(3\) fold onto a face already occupied and overlap it. Each of positions \(4,\) \(5,\) \(6,\) \(7,\) \(8,\) and \(9\) folds onto an unoccupied face. Therefore \(6\) of the nine positions work.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: A cube with one face missing needs \(5\) squares
Fold the four-square piece partway around a cube, then check which attached square lands on a still-open face
